_comment: klt erc supply spec for the gate_driver_core merged GDS -- the T1 item 11
(structural power delivery) evidence this repo records (issue #238),
graded per the Analog column: the klt erc supply-island read plus the
item-4 LVS report carrying every supply net in its net_correspondence
(verified: VDD_LOGIC/GND_LOGIC/VDD_DRV/GND_DRV each paired
layout<->reference with pin:true in
layout/lvs/reports/gate_driver_core/20260826-062806-a7dcce1.lvs.json).
Committed report:
python3 layout/erc/run_erc.py layout/gate_driver_core.gds \
--klt <path-to-klt-with-deck-device-subtraction>
(run_erc.py wraps the same invocation in both --format json and text,
under layout/erc/reports/gate_driver_core/<record-id>.erc.{json,txt};
<record-id> follows the shared layout/common/report_id.py convention.)
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` MUST carry `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own contract), so the
fabricators' stack starts at Poly2. `active_layer` (Comp 22/0) makes the
gate-area denominator `poly n diff` instead of raw poly area, which keeps
the uvlo bias network's 271 `ppolyf_u` unit-resistor bodies (poly with no
gate oxide, issue #221) out of `gates[]` entirely instead of reporting
non-physical antenna ratios for them (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md,
'Gate area').
- Metal1-Metal5 and all five vias are declared because this block's GDS
genuinely uses every one of them (klt layers: 3324 Contact shapes, 4855
Metal1, 200 Via1, 58 Metal2, 18 Via2, 32 Metal3, 2 Via3, 7 Metal4, 4
Via4, 2 Metal5): rails are Metal2, per-net left<->right jumpers are
Metal1, and the XCCOMP MIM option-B stack (issue #166) routes through
Metal3/Metal4 to its FuseTop top plates strapped on Metal5.
- `label_layer` belongs ONLY on Metal2 (36/10): a full-label survey of the
merged GDS finds all 50 text objects on 36/10 alone (25 nets x 2 rail
labels each; VDD_LOGIC/GND_LOGIC/VDD_DRV/GND_DRV among them) and zero on
any other layer. Unlike a standard-cell flow (PG pin text on 34/10, PDN
text on 81/10), this full-custom block writes supply pin text only where
its rails run, so declaring Metal1/Metal5 label layers would add
nothing.
- GDS layer numbers are gf180mcu's own drawn-layer numbers, cross-checked
against both sources issue #238 names: the PDK's own
libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp (Poly2 30/0, COMP 22/0, Contact
Via3 40/0, Metal4 46/0, Via4 41/0, Metal5 81/0) AND klayout-tools'
curated gf180mcu deck (decks/gf180mcu.py, which transcribes them from
the PDK's main.drc via derivations). The same triple is transcribed in
this repo's layout/gen_gate_driver_core.py.
- `nets[]`: all four supply pins of the design netlist are declared with
`kind: "supply"` (VDD_LOGIC / VDD_DRV rails, GND_LOGIC / GND_DRV
returns), which is what makes a VDD-GND short report as the severe
`erc.supply_short` rather than the general `erc.multiply_driven_net`.
Each must resolve to exactly ONE electrical island:
`erc.unconnected_net` fires on zero matches AND on more than one, so
ZERO findings of that rule is exactly the one-island-per-supply verdict.
Note the grounds: GND_LOGIC and GND_DRV are two pins but one
design-intent reference node only via a pad ring this bare core does
not draw (decision record 0001 Decision 1, layout/README.md 'two
grounds' note) -- in THIS GDS they are genuinely two separate islands,
which is exactly what the one-island-per-supply rule grades.
- There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and `erc.missing_tie`
is NOT COMPUTED by this run (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md: 'Omitted
entirely -> erc.missing_tie is never computed'): its zero count is an
absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. Two reasons, both
standing independently of the history (klayout-tools#2169's original
blanket-well collapse, since fixed there by isolating ties[] into
their own extraction): first, issue #238's directives ship this spec
without `ties[]`; second, this block's well-tap topology is not
expressible in the installed schema anyway -- a ties[] entry names
exactly ONE net, but this block's 30 Nwell shapes tie to TWO different
rails by region (VDD_LOGIC for the level shifter's PMOS, VDD_DRV for
the output stage's and uvlo's), so any single-net declaration reports
false `erc.missing_tie` on every well tied to the other rail, and the
native-substrate half has no drawn well layer to declare at all.
The well-tie evidence that stands in for the uncomputed rule is the
item-4 LVS closure: every one of the 1769 drawn transistors has a real,
drawn, contacted body tie to the schematic's own net (VDD_LOGIC/VDD_DRV
for the 664 PMOS, the deck's global substrate identity for the 1105
NMOS), klt lvs reports zero `device.body_unverified`, 2044/2044
devices / 295/295 nets / 25/25 pins matched (issue #132; report
20260826-062806-a7dcce1.lvs.json), plus drawn guard/substrate-tap
rings (PR #183) around each device region.
- The report is committed from a `--deck gf180mcu` run, which is load-
bearing: the uvlo's four bias strings (Rref/R1/R2/Rfb) are drawn
`ppolyf_u` devices that deliberately span VDD_DRV and GND_DRV
(design/netlist gate_driver_core.spice .subckt uvlo), and klt erc's
connectivity graph is device-blind -- without the deck's device-marker
subtraction those resistor bodies read as wires and the graph reports a
FALSE `erc.supply_short` between VDD_DRV and GND_DRV (the
mirror-image artifact documented as klayout-tools#2183 and fixed by
the devices[]/`--deck` mechanism, #2205/#2217; if the installed klt
predates `--deck` this is the error to expect). With --deck the
curated deck carves out exactly the 271 unit-resistor bodies
(9011.52 um2 of RES_MK-marked poly on 30/0) and the XCCOMP MIM plates,
echoed in provenance.devices with source "deck" -- and the supplies
grade on their real one-island connectivity, matching the LVS-
extracted reality of discrete 3-terminal devices rather than a metal
short.
- Antenna verdicts are intentionally NOT this spec's subject (item 11's
own text: an antenna finding is a real defect but does not block this
item); the committed run passes no `--pdk`, so `status` reads the
antenna rollup's `not_checked` while `erc_status` carries the supply
verdict this artifact exists for.
